title: Region-Specific EEG Classification of Hypnotic Susceptibility Using a Sliding-Window 2D CNN: A Subject-Independent Evaluation
summary: In 62 young adult men, frontal, parietal, and prefrontal regions retained modest above-chance classification (mean accuracy 0.646, 0.631, 0.624); occipital performance fell below chance (0.453) under subject-independent testing, indicating that random segment splits captured subject fingerprints. Leave-one-subject-out cross-validation across all 62 participants; 20-minute recordings. Results are exploratory because the cohort is small, all male, and aged 19–24; the paper is a v1 preprint.
ai_technology: A sliding-window 2D CNN classified hypnotic susceptibility from minimally preprocessed 256-channel EEG recordings and localized discriminative windows by brain region.
